facts.text: Asked if he believes Nvidia's highest-level processors have made it to China using the Singapore-based Megaspeed as a pass-through, Bessent said, "I think that there is a lot of leakage in the system, and we are constantly working to close that down."
"The story has been thus far on Jensen Huang's personal foibles," Bessent told CNBC.
Commerce Department spokeswoman Kristen Eichamer on Wednesday told CNBC that Bessent and Lutnick had "no such conversation" in the Situation Room.
Eichamer, the Commerce spokeswoman, told CNBC on Friday that Lutnick "has proactively agreed to appear voluntarily before the Banking Committee to address their questions."
The Commerce Department did not respond to CNBC's request for comment on Bessent's remarks.
Huang had pushed the U.S. government to ease restrictions on the export of advanced AI chips to China.

Washington Senator Maria Cantwell, one of the top Democrats on the Senate commerce committee, has taken fire at the Department of Commerce (DOC) under Secretary Howard Lutnick for neglecting to enforce protections intended to keep Nvidia’s AI chips away from China.

The DOC is also accused of “putting business interests ahead of national security,” with Cantwell noting that Cantor Fitzgerald, the financial services firm formerly led by Lutnick and now steered by his sons, reportedly held $1.2 billion in Nvidia stock at the time of Lutnick’s nomination for Commerce Secretary.

While Congress is looking to bolster export restrictions around AI chips, The Wall Street Journal reports that Lutnick is instead expected to unveil a new initiative that will designate Nvidia — along with companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon, and Microsoft — as an AI “national champion.” The designation reportedly aims to help these companies expand overseas and compete with Chinese technology firms by granting them expedited export licence approvals.

Cantwell also criticizes the DOC for allowing Alibaba and ByteDance to access Nvidia chips through overseas data centers, and extending a loophole that let restricted companies obtain American AI technology through subsidiaries.
The letter comes ahead of a meeting in China this Thursday between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
Cantwell called on Lutnick to use his authority under the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 to enforce export controls and stop the flow of AI chips to companies barred from receiving them [1] .
She sent the letter ahead of President Trump's meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in China on Thursday, Nov.
The Commerce Department did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment on Monday [1] .
AI chips from reaching China, CNBC and The Verge reported [1] [2] .
On conflicts, Cantwell said Cantor Fitzgerald, the firm Lutnick led and his sons now control, held $1.2 billion of Nvidia stock at the time of his nomination [1] .
She said the administration's 25% fee on certain Nvidia chips sold to China could create "a perverse financial incentive to approve exports of sensitive American technology" [1] .

"America's national security and AI leadership cannot be compromised by family business interests or a policy that generates federal revenue from exporting technology critical to our competitive edge," she wrote [1] .
Megaspeed has said Alice Huang left the company in August 2025 .
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said last week that the Megaspeed blacklisting stalled because Commerce "has the pen" .
Cantwell also criticized Commerce for letting Alibaba and ByteDance use Nvidia chips through overseas data centers and for extending a loophole that let restricted companies obtain U.S.

17 to confirm they have ordered Nvidia export records preserved [1] .
Lawmakers in both parties are also moving toward tighter AI chip export rules .

"The Administration must account for its failure to enforce these protections and take immediate action to prevent America's most sensitive technology from strengthening our adversaries," Cantwell wrote in closing [2] .
Separately, The Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday that the administration plans to name Nvidia and other U.S.
AI companies "national champions" to help them expand overseas.
